_meta.indication: VRAYLAR is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia and the acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose (placebo, cariprazine 3 mg/day, cariprazine 6 mg/day, aripiprazole 10 mg/day), with 6 weeks of double-blind treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=454 (cariprazine 3 mg/day N=151, cariprazine 6 mg/day N=154, aripiprazole 10 mg/day N=150, placebo N=149)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference from placebo in PANSS change: -6.0 (3 mg/day) and -8.8 (6 mg/day); adjusted p = 0.0044 (3 mg/day) and adjusted p < 0.0001 (6 mg/day)

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Cariprazine in Patients With Schizophrenia

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, fixed-dose, 6 weeks double-blind treatment; five arms (placebo, cariprazine 1.5, 3, 4.5 mg/day, risperidone 4.0 mg/day) in 1:1:1:1:1 ratio
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 6 in PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=573 (cariprazine 1.5 mg N=140, 3 mg N=140, 4.5 mg N=145, risperidone 4 mg N=138, placebo N=148)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference from placebo in PANSS change: -8.0 (1.5 mg), -8.2 (3 mg), -10.5 (4.5 mg); p = 0.0005 (1.5 mg), p < 0.0001 (3 mg), p < 0.0001 (4.5 mg)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, flexible-dose (1:1 placebo or cariprazine 3-12 mg/day), 3 weeks of double-blind treatment

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Cariprazine for Mania

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal bipolar mania study (one of three pivotal 3-week trials)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-flexible dose (1:1:1 placebo, cariprazine 3-6 mg/day, cariprazine 6-12 mg/day), 3 weeks double-blind treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 3 in YMRS total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=492 (cariprazine 3-6 mg/day N=165, cariprazine 6-12 mg/day N=167, placebo N=160)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference from placebo in YMRS change -6.1 (3-6 mg/day) and -5.9 (6-12 mg/day); adjusted p < 0.001 for YMRS for both dose ranges

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Cariprazine for Bipolar I Disorder

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 5% and at least twice the rate of placebo): in schizophrenia, extrapyramidal symptoms and akathisia; in bipolar mania, extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, dyspepsia, vomiting, somnolence, and restlessness. In 6-week schizophrenia trials extrapyramidal symptoms occurred in 17% of VRAYLAR patients versus 8% placebo, and akathisia 11% versus placebo.
target_moa: Atypical antipsychotic; efficacy may be mediated by partial agonist activity at dopamine D2 and D3 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and antagonist activity at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs; VRAYLAR is not approved for the treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis.

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial designs are similar to previously approved products and the safety profile is similar to other drugs approved for these indications.

description.text: Added two new strengths of Vraylar capsules

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the addition of two new strengths of Vraylar capsules (S-014), inclusion of pediatric patients 13 to 17 years of age for the treatment of schizophrenia (S-015), inclusion of pediatric patients 10 to 17 years of age for the acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder (S-016), and addition of the results from studies with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients to the prescribing information (S-017).

summary.text: Cariprazine was reviewed as a new molecular entity for treatment of schizophrenia and bipolar mania; FDA first issued a Complete Response Letter on November 19, 2013, and after resubmission (December 17, 2014) the NDA was approved September 17, 2015. No expedited-program designations were documented and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Cariprazine is a New Molecular Entity (NME) that has not been approved elsewhere in the world for any indication.

FDA issued a Complete Response (CR) Letter for the original application on November 19, 2013, citing significant dose-related toxicities identified in increasing frequency over time during the 6-week controlled trials.
The December 17, 2014, submission constituted a complete response to our November 19, 2013, action letter.

Your application for VRAYLAR was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial designs are similar to previously approved products for the acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder and the treatment of schizophrenia and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for these indications.
